units.function: Embedded-Postgres and real-filesystem integration test allowing local Company-skill imports only from configured workspace roots while rejecting out-of-tree paths, symlink escapes and non-HTTPS URL schemes.
units.dependencyDirection: Company/project/workspace rows define approved roots; an untrusted import source enters companySkillService, is canonicalized with realpath, checked against Company-scoped roots and then parsed/persisted as a Company skill.
units.keyDataModels: Company, Project, primary ProjectWorkspace cwd, local skill directory/SKILL.md, symbolic link and structured validation or boundary-denied error codes.
units.lifecycle: An in-workspace .agents/skills directory imports successfully; a real outside directory and an in-workspace symlink resolving outside are denied with 403; ftp/http sources are rejected with 422.
units.testAssessment: The test uses a real database and filesystem and strongly covers canonical path containment plus stable reason codes. Missing are a symlink-swap TOCTOU race between validation and recursive read, nested file symlinks, workspace-root mutation/revocation, case/Unicode/platform paths, permission failures, quotas, malicious SKILL.md content, HTTPS SSRF/download integrity, transaction rollback and actor/approval/audit evidence.
units.designRationale: Permit useful local imports from Company-configured workspaces without turning an arbitrary server filesystem path into an import capability.
units.companyOsProblem: FDE operators need controlled import from customer workspaces while self-hosted deployments must prevent filesystem escape, package substitution and cross-tenant ingestion.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT canonical Company-scoped root enforcement and stable error codes. Strengthen it by opening/copying through a sandboxed Connector node into immutable quarantine content, revalidating every entry without following links, hashing the package, scanning/license-checking it and binding approval plus provenance before publication.
units.responsibilityConflict: Workspace membership alone does not authorize importing executable instructions. The service call has no accountable human, data/tool contract or approval evidence, and realpath validation followed by later path-based reading leaves a substitution window.

units.function: Filesystem tests reconciling Codex runtime skill symlinks: repairing links to another Paperclip checkout, injecting missing requested skills, preserving custom or other live links and pruning broken links attributed to unavailable Paperclip skills.
units.dependencyDirection: A prepared skills home and requested key/runtime-name/source entries enter the Codex adapter reconciler; it classifies existing links using checkout/path heuristics, mutates symlinks and writes human-readable runtime logs.
units.keyDataModels: Canonical skill key, runtime name, source directory, current/old Paperclip checkout shape, custom external skill, live/broken symlink and injection/repair/removal log messages.
units.lifecycle: Before Codex starts, requested Paperclip links are created or repointed from an old live checkout; custom collisions and unrelated live Paperclip links are preserved; stale broken Paperclip links are removed.
units.testAssessment: The suite carefully protects custom collisions and exercises live, stale and cross-checkout link reconciliation. Missing are explicit ownership manifests, immutable digests, traversal/runtime-name validation, concurrent reconcilers, atomic replacement/crash recovery, permissions, required-skill failure behavior, cleanup after run, Windows behavior and proof of Codex activation.
units.designRationale: Repair stale development-checkout links without overwriting user-owned skills or deleting still-valid skills that share an execution home.
units.companyOsProblem: Connector nodes need safe reconciliation of leased capability packages without mistaking a pathname or repository layout for ownership.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the conservative preserve/repair/prune test matrix, but replace checkout heuristics with a signed installation manifest containing owner, package digest, lease, target and prior state; use atomic operations and emit structured activation/cleanup receipts.
units.responsibilityConflict: Path shape is used as an ownership proxy and cleanup is not tied to a Work lease. Repair/removal logs do not identify the approving human, package digest, policy grant or evidence chain and cannot prove temporary copies were destroyed.

units.function: Filesystem tests linking every source-directory child into Cursor's skill home, preserving existing targets and logging individual link failures while continuing.
units.dependencyDirection: A source directory, target skill home and optional link implementation enter the Cursor adapter reconciler; directory entries become symlinks and failures are converted to log text instead of rejecting startup.
units.keyDataModels: Source/target paths, directory entry name, symlink, preserved existing directory and per-skill success/failure log.
units.lifecycle: Missing directory entries are linked, non-directory files are ignored, existing targets remain untouched, and one failed link does not prevent other links or throw to the caller.
units.testAssessment: Happy-path materialization, collision preservation and partial-failure continuation are explicit. Missing are approved selection rather than all directories, package identity and provenance, runtime-name/path validation, symlink-source handling, atomicity/concurrency, required versus optional capability semantics, cleanup/revocation, structured error codes and runtime activation evidence.
units.designRationale: Keep Cursor startup resilient and avoid overwriting user-managed entries when convenience skill injection is partially unavailable.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must distinguish optional convenience capabilities from tools required by an approved Work plan; silently missing a required tool invalidates execution readiness.
units.companyOsFit: NARROW: preserve existing user targets and allow best-effort continuation only for explicitly optional packages. Required capability injection must fail closed with a stable code before Agent execution, and all packages must flow through the canonical signed SkillPackageManager rather than directory-wide discovery.
units.responsibilityConflict: The adapter can continue after a requested link fails, so the actual runtime capability set may differ from the approved plan. Free-form logs are not an attestation and no human grant, digest, Work binding or cleanup proof exists.
